You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "---
name: arc-copy-pattern-between-matching-frames
description: Use when ARC grids contain rectangular outline frames and one frame has an internal pattern. Copy that pattern into matching frames.
---

# Copy an interior pattern between matching frames

Use this rule when an ARC puzzle shows several rectangular frames (often different colors), with one frame containing nonzero cells inside its border and the rest blank inside.

1. Identify each frame's full rectangular bounding box, including the one-cell outline border.
2. Determine its interior dimensions: `(frame height - 2) × (frame width - 2)`.
3. Find the frame with a nonblank interior pattern. Treat its interior cells as the source pattern; do not include the frame border.
4. For every other frame with exactly the same interior dimensions, copy the source interior pattern cell-for-cell at the same relative row/column positions. Keep each destination's own border color intact.
5. Leave frames with different interior dimensions unchanged, and preserve all cells outside frames.
6. Verify dimensions and alignment carefully before submitting. A frame can appear filled/patterned only because its border has a colored outline; distinguish border from interior.

Evidence from task-54251d26: the patterned 7-frame had a 3×6 interior; blank 5- and 1-frames had matching 3×6 interiors and received the pattern. Other differently sized frames stayed unchanged. Demonstrations showed the same pattern propagation among matching interior sizes, while the source and nonmatching frames remained as they were.
",
